page.layout: One page of verse, one column, centred; running head at top; page number at top right; signature "B.iij." below the text at right; library stamp at bottom right (not transcribed).

p.i: Dum timor introrsus gemitúsque & verba retentat, Dum labor in veras cogit prorumpere voces, Editus in medys infans euagiit vndis. Pars facti nouitate stupet, quódque audiit ipsa Vix audisse putat: petulantior altera risu Personat: ast alius tumida succensus ab ira In mare precipitem monachū, & cum prole parentem Proturbare iubet, letóque abolere nefandum Dedecus; & monstro miseram releuare carinam. Hinc tumidos fluctus, pontóque furente procellas, Ventorúmque minas, & apertam Numinis iram. Si quis adest animi pius, & moderatior ira, Occultare cupit facinus, parcítque benignus Errori, humanos prudens expendere lapsus, Agnoscitque suas alieno in crimine vires.

main_text.p: Ergo dum trepidant discordia pectora vulgi, Nautarúmque fremit per littora rauca tumultus, Infelix frater turba sese infinuans clam Tramitibus caecis elabitur, orúque velans Vertice demisso peregrinas exul ad vrbes Moestus abit, poenáfque domi, famámque siniftram Formidans, miseráque gemens cum prole puellam, Quam solam, atque agram nuda licuisset in aëla, Inter inhumani risum & ludibria vulgi. Ipse ego tum validus, viridíque in flore iuuenta, Nec lingua nec vocis inops, nec flectere corda Plebis inexpertus stolida rumore secundo, Vix tamen aduersa glisentia murmura fama Flectere, vix potui populi compescere voces, Sape licet verbis factum execrarer amaris, Auctorem sceleris comitem licet esse Lutheri Iurarem sanctā latitantem nomine sectā.

page.notes: Scan is a mottled, faded page; the printed text is legible. The library stamp at lower right is not transcribed. Some words in the first and second lines of the verse may be affected by faint ink; "ast" and "aëla" are read as printed but uncertain.
